name: viewer-overlay
title: Viewer Overlay
description: A viewer over the whole window, e.g. a conversation's image, as a dialog: to the window's edges, one surface (no inset, corners or card in it). The app's viewer (a MediaViewer, or any ViewerFrame) fills it, its toolbar the window's top row (ViewerFrameTitlebar): as tall as an AgentApp's titlebar (--agent-app-titlebar, else 44px), past the window's own buttons (--agent-app-titlebar-inset), dragging the window but by its controls ([data-titlebar], app-region: drag; a host that drags it itself does so on a pointerdown there whose target is not a control); the viewer's name at its start, its facts after it, quieter (not in More, which is there only for the app's menu), then its lead (an image's versions and compare); at its end "Open in side panel" (where the app has a panel to move it to) and close (its own row with the overlay's label where the viewer has no toolbar). The viewer's tools are islands at the middle of its foot, over the composer and never over the image: marking (a mode whose tools, Clear marks and the send come after it) and the app's edits, then the zoom with the viewer's and the app's tools, add to chat, download and More; on two rows where they have no room on one. A strip of the conversation's images at the start, under the row (even of one; a placeholder for one with no thumbnail yet, the app loading it when it is picked, a spinner while `loading`) picking the one shown, its current one ringed and kept in view, gone on a phone; round buttons to the one before and after by the viewer's sides, with a mouse while it points at the viewer or one has focus, always under a finger and on a phone (the app gives its viewer no previous and next of its own); past a phone's status bar; and the app's composer under it, to ask about what is shown while it is. ← → go to the one before and after, where focus is not in a field, a menu or a slider.
